label: Shipping, Receiving, and Inventory Clerks
hint: Verify and maintain records on incoming and outgoing shipments involving inventory. Duties include verifying and recording incoming merchandise or material and arranging for the transportation of products. May prepare items for shipment.

label: Weighers, Measurers, Checkers, and Samplers, Recordkeeping
hint: Weigh, measure, and check materials, supplies, and equipment for the purpose of keeping relevant records. Duties are primarily clerical by nature. Includes workers who collect and keep record of samples of products or materials.

label: Executive Secretaries and Executive Administrative Assistants
hint: Provide high-level administrative support by conducting research, preparing statistical reports, and handling information requests, as well as performing routine administrative functions such as preparing correspondence, receiving visitors, arranging conference calls, and scheduling meetings. May also train and supervise lower-level clerical staff.

label: Legal Secretaries and Administrative Assistants
hint: Perform secretarial duties using legal terminology, procedures, and documents. Prepare legal papers and correspondence, such as summonses, complaints, motions, and subpoenas. May also assist with legal research.

label: Medical Secretaries and Administrative Assistants
hint: Perform secretarial duties using specific knowledge of medical terminology and hospital, clinic, or laboratory procedures. Duties may include scheduling appointments, billing patients, and compiling and recording medical charts, reports, and correspondence.

label: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive
hint: Perform routine administrative functions such as drafting correspondence, scheduling appointments, organizing and maintaining paper and electronic files, or providing information to callers.

label: Data Entry Keyers
hint: Operate data entry device, such as keyboard or photo composing perforator. Duties may include verifying data and preparing materials for printing.

label: Word Processors and Typists
hint: Use word processor, computer, or typewriter to type letters, reports, forms, or other material from rough draft, corrected copy, or voice recording. May perform other clerical duties as assigned.

label: Desktop Publishers
hint: Format typescript and graphic elements using computer software to produce publication-ready material.

label: Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks
hint: Process new insurance policies, modifications to existing policies, and claims forms. Obtain information from policyholders to verify the accuracy and completeness of information on claims forms, applications and related documents, and company records. Update existing policies and company records to reflect changes requested by policyholders and insurance company representatives.

label: Mail Clerks and Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service
hint: Prepare incoming and outgoing mail for distribution. Time-stamp, open, read, sort, and route incoming mail; and address, seal, stamp, fold, stuff, and affix postage to outgoing mail or packages. Duties may also include keeping necessary records and completed forms.

label: Office Clerks, General
hint: Perform duties too varied and diverse to be classified in any specific office clerical occupation, requiring knowledge of office systems and procedures. Clerical duties may be assigned in accordance with the office procedures of individual establishments and may include a combination of answering telephones, bookkeeping, typing or word processing, office machine operation, and filing.

label: Office Machine Operators, Except Computer
hint: Operate one or more of a variety of office machines, such as photocopying, photographic, and duplicating machines, or other office machines.

label: Proofreaders and Copy Markers
hint: Read transcript or proof type setup to detect and mark for correction any grammatical, typographical, or compositional errors. Excludes workers whose primary duty is editing copy. Includes proofreaders of braille.

label: Statistical Assistants
hint: Compile and compute data according to statistical formulas for use in statistical studies. May perform actuarial computations and compile charts and graphs for use by actuaries. Includes actuarial clerks.

label: Office and Administrative Support Workers, All Other
hint: All office and administrative support workers not listed separately.

hint: Inspect agricultural commodities, processing equipment, and facilities, and fish and logging operations, to ensure compliance with regulations and laws governing health, quality, and safety.

label: Animal Breeders
hint: Select and breed animals according to their genealogy, characteristics, and offspring. May require knowledge of artificial insemination techniques and equipment use. May involve keeping records on heats, birth intervals, or pedigree.

label: Graders and Sorters, Agricultural Products
hint: Grade, sort, or classify unprocessed food and other agricultural products by size, weight, color, or condition.

label: Agricultural Equipment Operators
hint: Drive and control equipment to support agricultural activities such as tilling soil; planting, cultivating, and harvesting crops; feeding and herding livestock; or removing animal waste. label: Farmworkers and Laborers, Crop, Nursery, and Greenhouse
hint: Manually plant, cultivate, and harvest vegetables, fruits, nuts, horticultural specialties, and field crops. label: Agricultural Workers, All Other
hint: All agricultural workers not listed separately.

label: Fishing and Hunting Workers
hint: Hunt, trap, catch, or gather wild animals or aquatic animals and plants. May use nets, traps, or other equipment. May haul catch onto ship or other vessel.

label: Forest and Conservation Workers
hint: Under supervision, perform manual labor necessary to develop, maintain, or protect areas such as forests, forested areas, woodlands, wetlands, and rangelands through such activities as raising and transporting seedlings; combating insects, pests, and diseases harmful to plant life; and building structures to control water, erosion, and leaching of soil. label: Fallers
hint: Use axes or chainsaws to fell trees using knowledge of tree characteristics and cutting techniques to control direction of fall and minimize tree damage.

label: Logging Equipment Operators
hint: Drive logging tractor or wheeled vehicle equipped with one or more accessories, such as bulldozer blade, frontal shear, grapple, logging arch, cable winches, hoisting rack, or crane boom, to fell tree; to skid, load, unload, or stack logs; or to pull stumps or clear brush. Includes operating stand-alone logging machines, such as log chippers.

label: Log Graders and Scalers
hint: Grade logs or estimate the marketable content or value of logs or pulpwood in sorting yards, millpond, log deck, or similar locations. Inspect logs for defects or measure logs to determine volume.

label: Logging Workers, All Other
hint: All logging workers not listed separately.

label: First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers
hint: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of construction or extraction workers.

label: Solar Energy Installation Managers
hint: Direct work crews installing residential or commercial solar photovoltaic or thermal systems.

label: Boilermakers
hint: Construct, assemble, maintain, and repair stationary steam boilers and boiler house auxiliaries. Align structures or plate sections to assemble boiler frame tanks or vats, following blueprints. Work involves use of hand and power tools, plumb bobs, levels, wedges, dogs, or turnbuckles. Assist in testing assembled vessels. Direct cleaning of boilers and boiler furnaces. Inspect and repair boiler fi

label: Brickmasons and Blockmasons
hint: Lay and bind building materials, such as brick, structural tile, concrete block, cinder block, glass block, and terra-cotta block, with mortar and other substances, to construct or repair walls, partitions, arches, sewers, and other structures.

label: Stonemasons
hint: Build stone structures, such as piers, walls, and abutments. Lay walks, curbstones, or special types of masonry for vats, tanks, and floors.

label: Carpenters
hint: Construct, erect, install, or repair structures and fixtures made of wood and comparable materials, such as concrete forms; building frameworks, including partitions, joists, studding, and rafters; and wood stairways, window and door frames, and hardwood floors. May also install cabinets, siding, drywall, and batt or roll insulation. Includes brattice builders who build doors or brattices (ventila

label: Carpet Installers
hint: Lay and install carpet from rolls or blocks on floors. Install padding and trim flooring materials.

label: Floor Layers, Except Carpet, Wood, and Hard Tiles
hint: Apply blocks, strips, or sheets of shock-absorbing, sound-deadening, or decorative coverings to floors.

label: Floor Sanders and Finishers
hint: Scrape and sand wooden floors to smooth surfaces using floor scraper and floor sanding machine, and apply coats of finish.

label: Tile and Stone Setters
hint: Apply hard tile, stone, and comparable materials to walls, floors, ceilings, countertops, and roof decks.

label: Cement Masons and Concrete Finishers
hint: Smooth and finish surfaces of poured concrete, such as floors, walks, sidewalks, roads, or curbs using a variety of hand and power tools. Align forms for sidewalks, curbs, or gutters; patch voids; and use saws to cut expansion joints.

label: Terrazzo Workers and Finishers
hint: Apply a mixture of cement, sand, pigment, or marble chips to floors, stairways, and cabinet fixtures to fashion durable and decorative surfaces.

label: Construction Laborers
hint: Perform tasks involving physical labor at construction sites. May operate hand and power tools of all types: air hammers, earth tampers, cement mixers, small mechanical hoists, surveying and measuring equipment, and a variety of other equipment and instruments. May clean and prepare sites, dig trenches, set braces to support the sides of excavations, erect scaffolding, and clean up rubble, debris,

label: Paving, Surfacing, and Tamping Equipment Operators
hint: Operate equipment used for applying concrete, asphalt, or other materials to road beds, parking lots, or airport runways and taxiways or for tamping gravel, dirt, or other materials. Includes concrete and asphalt paving machine operators, form tampers, tamping machine operators, and stone spreader operators.

label: Pile Driver Operators
hint: Operate pile drivers mounted on skids, barges, crawler treads, or locomotive cranes to drive pilings for retaining walls, bulkheads, and foundations of structures such as buildings, bridges, and piers.

label: Operating Engineers and Other Construction Equipment Operators
hint: Operate one or several types of power construction equipment, such as motor graders, bulldozers, scrapers, compressors, pumps, derricks, shovels, tractors, or front-end loaders to excavate, move, and grade earth, erect structures, or pour concrete or other hard surface pavement. May repair and maintain equipment in addition to other duties.

label: Drywall and Ceiling Tile Installers
hint: Apply plasterboard or other wallboard to ceilings or interior walls of buildings. Apply or mount acoustical tiles or blocks, strips, or sheets of shock-absorbing materials to ceilings and walls of buildings to reduce or reflect sound. Materials may be of decorative quality. Includes lathers who fasten wooden, metal, or rockboard lath to walls, ceilings, or partitions of buildings to provide suppor

label: Tapers
hint: Seal joints between plasterboard or other wallboard to prepare wall surface for painting or papering.

label: Electricians
hint: Install, maintain, and repair electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures. Ensure that work is in accordance with relevant codes. May install or service street lights, intercom systems, or electrical control systems.

label: Glaziers
hint: Install glass in windows, skylights, store fronts, and display cases, or on surfaces, such as building fronts, interior walls, ceilings, and tabletops.

label: Insulation Workers, Floor, Ceiling, and Wall
hint: Line and cover structures with insulating materials. May work with batt, roll, or blown insulation materials.

label: Insulation Workers, Mechanical
hint: Apply insulating materials to pipes or ductwork, or other mechanical systems in order to help control and maintain temperature.

label: Painters, Construction and Maintenance
hint: Paint walls, equipment, buildings, bridges, and other structural surfaces, using brushes, rollers, and spray guns. May remove old paint to prepare surface prior to painting. May mix colors or oils to obtain desired color or consistency.

label: Paperhangers
hint: Cover interior walls or ceilings of rooms with decorative wallpaper or fabric, or attach advertising posters on surfaces such as walls and billboards. May remove old materials or prepare surfaces to be papered.

label: Pipelayers
hint: Lay pipe for storm or sanitation sewers, drains, and water mains. Perform any combination of the following tasks: grade trenches or culverts, position pipe, or seal joints.

label: Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters
hint: Assemble, install, alter, and repair pipelines or pipe systems that carry water, steam, air, or other liquids or gases. May install heating and cooling equipment and mechanical control systems. Includes sprinkler fitters.

label: Solar Thermal Installers and Technicians
hint: Install or repair solar energy systems designed to collect, store, and circulate solar-heated water for residential, commercial or industrial use.

label: Plasterers and Stucco Masons
hint: Apply interior or exterior plaster, cement, stucco, or similar materials. May also set ornamental plaster.

label: Reinforcing Iron and Rebar Workers
hint: Position and secure steel bars or mesh in concrete forms in order to reinforce concrete. Use a variety of fasteners, rod-bending machines, blowtorches, and hand tools. Includes rod busters.

label: Roofers
hint: Cover roofs of structures with shingles, slate, asphalt, aluminum, wood, or related materials. May spray roofs, sidings, and walls with material to bind, seal, insulate, or soundproof sections of structures.

label: Sheet Metal Workers
hint: Fabricate, assemble, install, and repair sheet metal products and equipment, such as ducts, control boxes, drainpipes, and furnace casings. Work may involve any of the following: setting up and operating fabricating machines to cut, bend, and straighten sheet metal; shaping metal over anvils, blocks, or forms using hammer; operating soldering and welding equipment to join sheet metal parts; or ins

label: Structural Iron and Steel Workers
hint: Raise, place, and unite iron or steel girders, columns, and other structural members to form completed structures or structural frameworks. May erect metal storage tanks and assemble prefabricated metal buildings.

label: Solar Photovoltaic Installers
hint: Assemble, install, or maintain solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on roofs or other structures in compliance with site assessment and schematics. May include measuring, cutting, assembling, and bolting structural framing and solar modules. May perform minor electrical work such as current checks.

label: Helpers--Brickmasons, Blockmasons, Stonemasons, and Tile and Marble Setters
hint: Help brickmasons, blockmasons, stonemasons, or tile and marble setters by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

label: Helpers--Carpenters
hint: Help carpenters by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

label: Helpers--Electricians
hint: Help electricians by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

label: Helpers--Painters, Paperhangers, Plasterers, and Stucco Masons
hint: Help painters, paperhangers, plasterers, or stucco masons by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

label: Helpers--Pipelayers, Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters
hint: Help plumbers, pipefitters, steamfitters, or pipelayers by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

label: Helpers--Roofers
hint: Help roofers by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

label: Helpers, Construction Trades, All Other
hint: All construction trades helpers not listed separately.

label: Construction and Building Inspectors
hint: Inspect structures using engineering skills to determine structural soundness and compliance with specifications, building codes, and other regulations. Inspections may be general in nature or may be limited to a specific area, such as electrical systems or plumbing.

label: Energy Auditors
hint: Conduct energy audits of buildings, building systems, or process systems. May also conduct investment grade audits of buildings or systems.

label: Elevator and Escalator Installers and Repairers
hint: Assemble, install, repair, or maintain electric or hydraulic freight or passenger elevators, escalators, or dumbwaiters.

label: Fence Erectors
hint: Erect and repair fences and fence gates, using hand and power tools.

label: Hazardous Materials Removal Workers
hint: Identify, remove, pack, transport, or dispose of hazardous materials, including asbestos, lead-based paint, waste oil, fuel, transmission fluid, radioactive materials, or contaminated soil. Specialized training and certification in hazardous materials handling or a confined entry permit are generally required. May operate earth-moving equipment or trucks.

label: Highway Maintenance Workers
hint: Maintain highways, municipal and rural roads, airport runways, and rights-of-way. Duties include patching broken or eroded pavement and repairing guard rails, highway markers, and snow fences. May also mow or clear brush from along road, or plow snow from roadway.

label: Rail-Track Laying and Maintenance Equipment Operators
hint: Lay, repair, and maintain track for standard or narrow-gauge railroad equipment used in regular railroad service or in plant yards, quarries, sand and gravel pits, and mines. Includes ballast cleaning machine operators and railroad bed tamping machine operators.

label: Septic Tank Servicers and Sewer Pipe Cleaners
hint: Clean and repair septic tanks, sewer lines, or drains. May patch walls and partitions of tank, replace damaged drain tile, or repair breaks in underground piping.

label: Segmental Pavers
hint: Lay out, cut, and place segmental paving units. Includes installers of bedding and restraining materials for the paving units.

label: Construction and Related Workers, All Other
hint: All construction and related workers not listed separately.

label: Weatherization Installers and Technicians
hint: Perform a variety of activities to weatherize homes and make them more energy efficient. Duties include repairing windows, insulating ducts, and performing heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning (HVAC) work. May perform energy audits and advise clients on energy conservation measures.

label: Derrick Operators, Oil and Gas
hint: Rig derrick equipment and operate pumps to circulate mud or fluid through drill hole.

label: Rotary Drill Operators, Oil and Gas
hint: Set up or operate a variety of drills to remove underground oil and gas, or remove core samples for testing during oil and gas exploration.

label: Service Unit Operators, Oil and Gas
hint: Operate equipment to increase oil flow from producing wells or to remove stuck pipe, casing, tools, or other obstructions from drilling wells. Includes fishing-tool technicians.

label: Excavating and Loading Machine and Dragline Operators, Surface Mining
hint: Operate or tend machinery at surface mining site, equipped with scoops, shovels, or buckets to excavate and load loose materials.

label: Earth Drillers, Except Oil and Gas
hint: Operate a variety of drills such as rotary, churn, and pneumatic to tap subsurface water and salt deposits, to remove core samples during mineral exploration or soil testing, and to facilitate the use of explosives in mining or construction. Includes horizontal and earth boring machine operators.

label: Explosives Workers, Ordnance Handling Experts, and Blasters
hint: Place and detonate explosives to demolish structures or to loosen, remove, or displace earth, rock, or other materials. May perform specialized handling, storage, and accounting procedures.

label: Continuous Mining Machine Operators
hint: Operate self-propelled mining machines that rip coal, metal and nonmetal ores, rock, stone, or sand from the mine face and load it onto conveyors, shuttle cars, or trucks in a continuous operation.

label: Roof Bolters, Mining
hint: Operate machinery to install roof support bolts in underground mine.

label: Loading and Moving Machine Operators, Underground Mining
hint: Operate underground loading or moving machine to load or move coal, ore, or rock using shuttle or mine car or conveyors. Equipment may include power shovels, hoisting engines equipped with cable-drawn scraper or scoop, or machines equipped with gathering arms and conveyor.

label: Underground Mining Machine Operators, All Other
hint: All underground mining machine operators not listed separately.

label: Rock Splitters, Quarry
hint: Separate blocks of rough dimension stone from quarry mass using jackhammers, wedges, or chop saws.

label: Roustabouts, Oil and Gas
hint: Assemble or repair oil field equipment using hand and power tools. Perform other tasks as needed.

label: Helpers--Extraction Workers
hint: Help extraction craft workers, such as earth drillers, blasters and explosives workers, derrick operators, and mining machine operators, by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include supplying equipment or cleaning work area.

label: Extraction Workers, All Other
hint: All extraction workers not listed separately.

label: First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
hint: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of mechanics, installers, and repairers. May also advise customers on recommended services. Excludes team or work leaders.

label: Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers
hint: Repair, maintain, or install computers, word processing systems, automated teller machines, and electronic office machines, such as duplicating and fax machines.

label: Radio, Cellular, and Tower Equipment Installers and Repairers
hint: Repair, install, or maintain mobile or stationary radio transmitting, broadcasting, and receiving equipment, and two-way radio communications systems used in cellular telecommunications, mobile broadband, ship-to-shore, aircraft-to-ground communications, and radio equipment in service and emergency vehicles. May test and analyze network coverage.

label: Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers, Except Line Installers
hint: Install, set up, rearrange, or remove switching, distribution, routing, and dialing equipment used in central offices or headends. Service or repair telephone, cable television, Internet, and other communications equipment on customers' property. May install communications equipment or communications wiring in buildings.

label: Avionics Technicians
hint: Install, inspect, test, adjust, or repair avionics equipment, such as radar, radio, navigation, and missile control systems in aircraft or space vehicles.

label: Electric Motor, Power Tool, and Related Repairers
hint: Repair, maintain, or install electric motors, wiring, or switches.

label: Electrical and Electronics Installers and Repairers, Transportation Equipment
hint: Install, adjust, or maintain mobile electronics communication equipment, including sound, sonar, security, navigation, and surveillance systems on trains, watercraft, or other mobile equipment.

label: Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Commercial and Industrial Equipment
hint: Repair, test, adjust, or install electronic equipment, such as industrial controls, transmitters, and antennas.

label: Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Powerhouse, Substation, and Relay
hint: Inspect, test, repair, or maintain electrical equipment in generating stations, substations, and in-service relays.

label: Electronic Equipment Installers and Repairers, Motor Vehicles
hint: Install, diagnose, or repair communications, sound, security, or navigation equipment in motor vehicles.

label: Audiovisual Equipment Installers and Repairers
hint: Install, repair, or adjust audio or television receivers, stereo systems, camcorders, video systems, or other electronic entertainment equipment in homes or other venues. May perform routine maintenance.

label: Security and Fire Alarm Systems Installers
hint: Install, program, maintain, and repair security and fire alarm wiring and equipment. Ensure that work is in accordance with relevant codes.

label: Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians
hint: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul aircraft engines and assemblies, such as hydraulic and pneumatic systems.

label: Automotive Body and Related Repairers
hint: Repair and refinish automotive vehicle bodies and straighten vehicle frames.

label: Automotive Glass Installers and Repairers
hint: Replace or repair broken windshields and window glass in motor vehicles.

label: Automotive Service Technicians and Mechanics
hint: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul automotive vehicles.

label: Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists
hint: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul buses and trucks, or maintain and repair any type of diesel engines. Includes mechanics working primarily with automobile or marine diesel engines.

label: Farm Equipment Mechanics and Service Technicians
hint: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul farm machinery and vehicles, such as tractors, harvesters, dairy equipment, and irrigation systems.

label: Mobile Heavy Equipment Mechanics, Except Engines
hint: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul mobile mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic equipment, such as cranes, bulldozers, graders, and conveyors, used in construction, logging, and mining.

label: Rail Car Repairers
hint: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul railroad rolling stock, mine cars, or mass transit rail cars.

label: Motorboat Mechanics and Service Technicians
hint: Repair and adjust electrical and mechanical equipment of inboard or inboard-outboard boat engines.

label: Motorcycle Mechanics
hint: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul motorcycles, scooters, mopeds, dirt bikes, or similar motorized vehicles.

label: Outdoor Power Equipment and Other Small Engine Mechanics
hint: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul small engines used to power lawn mowers, chain saws, recreational sporting equipment, and related equipment.

label: Bicycle Repairers
hint: Repair and service bicycles.

label: Recreational Vehicle Service Technicians
hint: Diagnose, inspect, adjust, repair, or overhaul recreational vehicles including travel trailers. May specialize in maintaining gas, electrical, hydraulic, plumbing, or chassis/towing systems as well as repairing generators, appliances, and interior components. Includes workers who perform customized van conversions.

label: Tire Repairers and Changers
hint: Repair and replace tires.

label: Mechanical Door Repairers
hint: Install, service, or repair automatic door mechanisms and hydraulic doors. Includes garage door mechanics.

label: Control and Valve Installers and Repairers, Except Mechanical Door
hint: Install, repair, and maintain mechanical regulating and controlling devices, such as electric meters, gas regulators, thermostats, safety and flow valves, and other mechanical governors.

label: Heating, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration Mechanics and Installers
hint: Install or repair heating, central air conditioning, HVAC, or refrigeration systems, including oil burners, hot-air furnaces, and heating stoves.

label: Home Appliance Repairers
hint: Repair, adjust, or install all types of electric or gas household appliances, such as refrigerators, washers, dryers, and ovens.

label: Industrial Machinery Mechanics
hint: Repair, install, adjust, or maintain industrial production and processing machinery or refinery and pipeline distribution systems. May also install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to plans.

label: Maintenance Workers, Machinery
hint: Lubricate machinery, change parts, or perform other routine machinery maintenance.

label: Millwrights
hint: Install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to layout plans, blueprints, or other drawings.

label: Refractory Materials Repairers, Except Brickmasons
hint: Build or repair equipment such as furnaces, kilns, cupolas, boilers, converters, ladles, soaking pits, and ovens, using refractory materials.

label: Electrical Power-Line Installers and Repairers
hint: Install or repair cables or wires used in electrical power or distribution systems. May erect poles and light or heavy duty transmission towers.

label: Telecommunications Line Installers and Repairers
hint: Install and repair telecommunications cable, including fiber optics.

label: Camera and Photographic Equipment Repairers
hint: Repair and adjust cameras and photographic equipment, including commercial video and motion picture camera equipment.

label: Medical Equipment Repairers
hint: Test, adjust, or repair biomedical or electromedical equipment.

label: Musical Instrument Repairers and Tuners
hint: Repair percussion, stringed, reed, or wind instruments. May specialize in one area, such as piano tuning.

label: Watch and Clock Repairers
hint: Repair, clean, and adjust mechanisms of timing instruments, such as watches and clocks. Includes watchmakers, watch technicians, and mechanical timepiece repairers.

label: Precision Instrument and Equipment Repairers, All Other
hint: All precision instrument and equipment repairers not listed separately.

label: Maintenance and Repair Workers, General
hint: Perform work involving the skills of two or more maintenance or craft occupations to keep machines, mechanical equipment, or the structure of a building in repair. Duties may involve pipe fitting; HVAC maintenance; insulating; welding; machining; carpentry; repairing electrical or mechanical equipment; installing, aligning, and balancing new equipment; and repairing buildings, floors, or stairs.

label: Wind Turbine Service Technicians
hint: Inspect, diagnose, adjust, or repair wind turbines. Perform maintenance on wind turbine equipment including resolving electrical, mechanical, and hydraulic malfunctions.

label: Coin, Vending, and Amusement Machine Servicers and Repairers
hint: Install, service, adjust, or repair coin, vending, or amusement machines including video games, juke boxes, pinball machines, or slot machines.

label: Commercial Divers
hint: Work below surface of water, using surface-supplied air or scuba equipment to inspect, repair, remove, or install equipment and structures. May use a variety of power and hand tools, such as drills, sledgehammers, torches, and welding equipment. May conduct tests or experiments, rig explosives, or photograph structures or marine life.

label: Locksmiths and Safe Repairers
hint: Repair and open locks, make keys, change locks and safe combinations, and install and repair safes.

label: Manufactured Building and Mobile Home Installers
hint: Move or install mobile homes or prefabricated buildings.

label: Riggers
hint: Set up or repair rigging for construction projects, manufacturing plants, logging yards, ships and shipyards, or for the entertainment industry.

label: Signal and Track Switch Repairers
hint: Install, inspect, test, maintain, or repair electric gate crossings, signals, signal equipment, track switches, section lines, or intercommunications systems within a railroad system.

label: Helpers--Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers
hint: Help installation, maintenance, and repair workers in maintenance, parts replacement, and repair of vehicles, industrial machinery, and electrical and electronic equipment. Perform duties such as furnishing tools, materials, and supplies to other workers; cleaning work area, machines, and tools; and holding materials or tools for other workers.

label: Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers, All Other
hint: All installation, maintenance, and repair workers not listed separately.

label: Geothermal Technicians
hint: Perform technical activities at power plants or individual installations necessary for the generation of power from geothermal energy sources. Monitor and control operating activities at geothermal power generation facilities and perform maintenance and repairs as necessary. Install, test, and maintain residential and commercial geothermal heat pumps.

label: First-Line Supervisors of Production and Operating Workers
hint: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of production and operating workers, such as inspectors, precision workers, machine setters and operators, assemblers, fabricators, and plant and system operators. Excludes team or work leaders.

label: Aircraft Structure, Surfaces, Rigging, and Systems Assemblers
hint: Assemble, fit, fasten, and install parts of airplanes, space vehicles, or missiles, such as tails, wings, fuselage, bulkheads, stabilizers, landing gear, rigging and control equipment, or heating and ventilating systems.

label: Coil Winders, Tapers, and Finishers
hint: Wind wire coils used in electrical components, such as resistors and transformers, and in electrical equipment and instruments, such as field cores, bobbins, armature cores, electrical motors, generators, and control equipment.

label: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Assemblers
hint: Assemble or modify electrical or electronic equipment, such as computers, test equipment telemetering systems, electric motors, and batteries.

label: Electromechanical Equipment Assemblers
hint: Assemble or modify electromechanical equipment or devices, such as servomechanisms, gyros, dynamometers, magnetic drums, tape drives, brakes, control linkage, actuators, and appliances.

label: Engine and Other Machine Assemblers
hint: Construct, assemble, or rebuild machines, such as engines, turbines, and similar equipment used in such industries as construction, extraction, textiles, and paper manufacturing.

label: Structural Metal Fabricators and Fitters
hint: Fabricate, position, align, and fit parts of structural metal products.

label: Fiberglass Laminators and Fabricators
hint: Laminate layers of fiberglass on molds to form boat decks and hulls, bodies for golf carts, automobiles, or other products.

label: Timing Device Assemblers and Adjusters
hint: Perform precision assembling or adjusting, within narrow tolerances, of timing devices such as digital clocks or timing devices with electrical or electronic components.

label: Team Assemblers
hint: Work as part of a team having responsibility for assembling an entire product or component of a product. Team assemblers can perform all tasks conducted by the team in the assembly process and rotate through all or most of them, rather than being assigned to a specific task on a permanent basis. May participate in making management decisions affecting the work. Includes team leaders who work as pa

label: Assemblers and Fabricators, All Other
hint: All assemblers and fabricators not listed separately.

label: Bakers
hint: Mix and bake ingredients to produce breads, rolls, cookies, cakes, pies, pastries, or other baked goods.

label: Butchers and Meat Cutters
hint: Cut, trim, or prepare consumer-sized portions of meat for use or sale in retail establishments.

label: Meat, Poultry, and Fish Cutters and Trimmers
hint: Use hands or hand tools to perform routine cutting and trimming of meat, poultry, and seafood.

label: Slaughterers and Meat Packers
hint: Perform nonroutine or precision functions involving the preparation of large portions of meat. Work may include specialized slaughtering tasks, cutting standard or premium cuts of meat for marketing, making sausage, or wrapping meats. Work typically occurs in slaughtering, meat packing, or wholesale establishments.

label: Food and Tobacco Roasting, Baking, and Drying Machine Operators and Tenders
hint: Operate or tend food or tobacco roasting, baking, or drying equipment, including hearth ovens, kiln driers, roasters, char kilns, and vacuum drying equipment.

label: Food Batchmakers
hint: Set up and operate equipment that mixes or blends ingredients used in the manufacturing of food products. Includes candy makers and cheese makers.

label: Food Cooking Machine Operators and Tenders
hint: Operate or tend cooking equipment, such as steam cooking vats, deep fry cookers, pressure cookers, kettles, and boilers, to prepare food products.

label: Food Processing Workers, All Other
hint: All food processing workers not listed separately.

label: Extruding and Drawing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
hint: Set up, operate, or tend machines to extrude or draw thermoplastic or metal materials into tubes, rods, hoses, wire, bars, or structural shapes.

label: Forging Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
hint: Set up, operate, or tend forging machines to taper, shape, or form metal or plastic parts.

label: Rolling Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
hint: Set up, operate, or tend machines to roll steel or plastic forming bends, beads, knurls, rolls, or plate, or to flatten, temper, or reduce gauge of material.

label: Cutting, Punching, and Press Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
hint: Set up, operate, or tend machines to saw, cut, shear, slit, punch, crimp, notch, bend, or straighten metal or plastic material.

label: Drilling and Boring Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
hint: Set up, operate, or tend drilling machines to drill, bore, ream, mill, or countersink metal or plastic work pieces.

label: Grinding, Lapping, Polishing, and Buffing Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
hint: Set up, operate, or tend grinding and related tools that remove excess material or burrs from surfaces, sharpen edges or corners, or buff, hone, or polish metal or plastic work pieces.

label: Lathe and Turning Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
hint: Set up, operate, or tend lathe and turning machines to turn, bore, thread, form, or face metal or plastic materials, such as wire, rod, or bar stock.

label: Milling and Planing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
hint: Set up, operate, or tend milling or planing machines to mill, plane, shape, groove, or profile metal or plastic work pieces.

label: Machinists
hint: Set up and operate a variety of machine tools to produce precision parts and instruments out of metal. Includes precision instrument makers who fabricate, modify, or repair mechanical instruments. May also fabricate and modify parts to make or repair machine tools or maintain industrial machines, applying knowledge of mechanics, mathematics, metal properties, layout, and machining procedures.

label: Metal-Refining Furnace Operators and Tenders
hint: Operate or tend furnaces, such as gas, oil, coal, electric-arc or electric induction, open-hearth, or oxygen furnaces, to melt and refine metal before casting or to produce specified types of steel.

label: Pourers and Casters, Metal
hint: Operate hand-controlled mechanisms to pour and regulate the flow of molten metal into molds to produce castings or ingots.

label: Model Makers, Metal and Plastic
hint: Set up and operate machines, such as lathes, milling and engraving machines, and jig borers to make working models of metal or plastic objects. Includes template makers.

label: Patternmakers, Metal and Plastic
hint: Lay out, machine, fit, and assemble castings and parts to metal or plastic foundry patterns, core boxes, or match plates.

label: Foundry Mold and Coremakers
hint: Make or form wax or sand cores or molds used in the production of metal castings in foundries.

label: Molding, Coremaking, and Casting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
hint: Set up, operate, or tend metal or plastic molding, casting, or coremaking machines to mold or cast metal or thermoplastic parts or products.

label: Multiple Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
hint: Set up, operate, or tend more than one type of cutting or forming machine tool or robot.

label: Tool and Die Makers
hint: Analyze specifications, lay out metal stock, set up and operate machine tools, and fit and assemble parts to make and repair dies, cutting tools, jigs, fixtures, gauges, and machinists' hand tools.

label: Welders, Cutters, Solderers, and Brazers
hint: Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products.

label: Welding, Soldering, and Brazing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
hint: Set up, operate, or tend welding, soldering, or brazing machines or robots that weld, braze, solder, or heat treat metal products, components, or assemblies. Includes workers who operate laser cutters or laser-beam machines.

label: Heat Treating Equipment Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
hint: Set up, operate, or tend heating equipment, such as heat-treating furnaces, flame-hardening machines, induction machines, soaking pits, or vacuum equipment to temper, harden, anneal, or heat treat metal or plastic objects.

label: Layout Workers, Metal and Plastic
hint: Lay out reference points and dimensions on metal or plastic stock or workpieces, such as sheets, plates, tubes, structural shapes, castings, or machine parts, for further processing. Includes shipfitters.

label: Plating Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
hint: Set up, operate, or tend plating machines to coat metal or plastic products with chromium, zinc, copper, cadmium, nickel, or other metal to protect or decorate surfaces. Typically, the product being coated is immersed in molten metal or an electrolytic solution.

label: Tool Grinders, Filers, and Sharpeners
hint: Perform precision smoothing, sharpening, polishing, or grinding of metal objects.

label: Metal Workers and Plastic Workers, All Other
hint: All metal workers and plastic workers not listed separately.

label: Prepress Technicians and Workers
hint: Format and proof text and images submitted by designers and clients into finished pages that can be printed. Includes digital and photo typesetting. May produce printing plates.

label: Printing Press Operators
hint: Set up and operate digital, letterpress, lithographic, flexographic, gravure, or other printing machines. Includes short-run offset printing presses.

label: Print Binding and Finishing Workers
hint: Bind books and other publications or finish printed products by hand or machine. May set up binding and finishing machines.

label: Laundry and Dry-Cleaning Workers
hint: Operate or tend washing or dry-cleaning machines to wash or dry-clean industrial or household articles, such as cloth garments, suede, leather, furs, blankets, draperies, linens, rugs, and carpets. Includes spotters and dyers of these articles.

label: Pressers, Textile, Garment, and Related Materials
hint: Press or shape articles by hand or machine.

label: Sewing Machine Operators
hint: Operate or tend sewing machines to join, reinforce, decorate, or perform related sewing operations in the manufacture of garment or nongarment products.

label: Shoe and Leather Workers and Repairers
hint: Construct, decorate, or repair leather and leather-like products, such as luggage, shoes, and saddles. May use hand tools.

label: Shoe Machine Operators and Tenders
hint: Operate or tend a variety of machines to join, decorate, reinforce, or finish shoes and shoe parts.

label: Sewers, Hand
hint: Sew, join, reinforce, or finish, usually with needle and thread, a variety of manufactured items. Includes weavers and stitchers.

label: Tailors, Dressmakers, and Custom Sewers
hint: Design, make, alter, repair, or fit garments.

label: Textile Bleaching and Dyeing Machine Operators and Tenders
hint: Operate or tend machines to bleach, shrink, wash, dye, or finish textiles or synthetic or glass fibers.

label: Textile Cutting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
hint: Set up, operate, or tend machines that cut textiles.

label: Textile Knitting and Weaving Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
hint: Set up, operate, or tend machines that knit, loop, weave, or draw in textiles.

label: Textile Winding, Twisting, and Drawing Out Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
hint: Set up, operate, or tend machines that wind or twist textiles; or draw out and combine sliver, such as wool, hemp, or synthetic fibers. Includes slubber machine and drawing frame operators.

label: Extruding and Forming Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Synthetic and Glass Fibers
hint: Set up, operate, or tend machines that extrude and form continuous filaments from synthetic materials, such as liquid polymer, rayon, and fiberglass.

label: Fabric and Apparel Patternmakers
hint: Draw and construct sets of precision master fabric patterns or layouts. May also mark and cut fabrics and apparel.

label: Upholsterers
hint: Make, repair, or replace upholstery for household furniture or transportation vehicles.

label: Textile, Apparel, and Furnishings Workers, All Other
hint: All textile, apparel, and furnishings workers not listed separately.

label: Cabinetmakers and Bench Carpenters
hint: Cut, shape, and assemble wooden articles or set up and operate a variety of woodworking machines, such as power saws, jointers, and mortisers to surface, cut, or shape lumber or to fabricate parts for wood products.

label: Furniture Finishers
hint: Shape, finish, and refinish damaged, worn, or used furniture or new high-grade furniture to specified color or finish.

label: Model Makers, Wood
hint: Construct full-size and scale wooden precision models of products. Includes wood jig builders and loft workers.

label: Patternmakers, Wood
hint: Plan, lay out, and construct wooden unit or sectional patterns used in forming sand molds for castings.

label: Sawing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Wood
hint: Set up, operate, or tend wood sawing machines. May operate computer numerically controlled (CNC) equipment. Includes lead sawyers.

label: Woodworking Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Except Sawing
hint: Set up, operate, or tend woodworking machines, such as drill presses, lathes, shapers, routers, sanders, planers, and wood nailing machines. May operate computer numerically controlled (CNC) equipment.

label: Woodworkers, All Other
hint: All woodworkers not listed separately.

label: Nuclear Power Reactor Operators
hint: Operate or control nuclear reactors. Move control rods, start and stop equipment, monitor and adjust controls, and record data in logs. Implement emergency procedures when needed. May respond to abnormalities, determine cause, and recommend corrective action.

label: Power Distributors and Dispatchers
hint: Coordinate, regulate, or distribute electricity or steam.

label: Power Plant Operators
hint: Control, operate, or maintain machinery to generate electric power. Includes auxiliary equipment operators.

label: Biomass Plant Technicians
hint: Control and monitor biomass plant activities and perform maintenance as needed.

label: Hydroelectric Plant Technicians
hint: Monitor and control activities associated with hydropower generation. Operate plant equipment, such as turbines, pumps, valves, gates, fans, electric control boards, and battery banks. Monitor equipment operation and performance and make necessary adjustments to ensure optimal performance. Perform equipment maintenance and repair as necessary.

label: Stationary Engineers and Boiler Operators
hint: Operate or maintain stationary engines, boilers, or other mechanical equipment to provide utilities for buildings or industrial processes. Operate equipment such as steam engines, generators, motors, turbines, and steam boilers.

label: Water and Wastewater Treatment Plant and System Operators
hint: Operate or control an entire process or system of machines, often through the use of control boards, to transfer or treat water or wastewater.

label: Chemical Plant and System Operators
hint: Control or operate entire chemical processes or system of machines.

label: Gas Plant Operators
hint: Distribute or process gas for utility companies and others by controlling compressors to maintain specified pressures on main pipelines.

label: Petroleum Pump System Operators, Refinery Operators, and Gaugers
hint: Operate or control petroleum refining or processing units. May specialize in controlling manifold and pumping systems, gauging or testing oil in storage tanks, or regulating the flow of oil into pipelines.

label: Plant and System Operators, All Other
hint: All plant and system operators not listed separately.

label: Biofuels Processing Technicians
hint: Calculate, measure, load, mix, and process refined feedstock with additives in fermentation or reaction process vessels and monitor production process. Perform, and keep records of, plant maintenance, repairs, and safety inspections.

label: Chemical Equipment Operators and Tenders
hint: Operate or tend equipment to control chemical changes or reactions in the processing of industrial or consumer products. Equipment used includes devulcanizers, steam-jacketed kettles, and reactor vessels.

label: Separating, Filtering, Clarifying, Precipitating, and Still Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
hint: Set up, operate, or tend continuous flow or vat-type equipment; filter presses; shaker screens; centrifuges; condenser tubes; precipitating, fermenting, or evaporating tanks; scrubbing towers; or batch stills. These machines extract, sort, or separate liquids, gases, or solids from other materials to recover a refined product. Includes dairy processing equipment operators.

label: Crushing, Grinding, and Polishing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
hint: Set up, operate, or tend machines to crush, grind, or polish materials, such as coal, glass, grain, stone, food, or rubber.

label: Grinding and Polishing Workers, Hand
hint: Grind, sand, or polish, using hand tools or hand-held power tools, a variety of metal, wood, stone, clay, plastic, or glass objects. Includes chippers, buffers, and finishers.

label: Mixing and Blending Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
hint: Set up, operate, or tend machines to mix or blend materials, such as chemicals, tobacco, liquids, color pigments, or explosive ingredients.

label: Cutters and Trimmers, Hand
hint: Use hand tools or hand-held power tools to cut and trim a variety of manufactured items, such as carpet, fabric, stone, glass, or rubber.

label: Cutting and Slicing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
hint: Set up, operate, or tend machines that cut or slice materials, such as glass, stone, cork, rubber, tobacco, food, paper, or insulating material.

label: Extruding, Forming, Pressing, and Compacting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
hint: Set up, operate, or tend machines, such as glass-forming machines, plodder machines, and tuber machines, to shape and form products such as glassware, food, rubber, soap, brick, tile, clay, wax, tobacco, or cosmetics.

label: Furnace, Kiln, Oven, Drier, and Kettle Operators and Tenders
hint: Operate or tend heating equipment other than basic metal, plastic, or food processing equipment. Includes activities such as annealing glass, drying lumber, curing rubber, removing moisture from materials, or boiling soap.

label: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
hint: Inspect, test, sort, sample, or weigh nonagricultural raw materials or processed, machined, fabricated, or assembled parts or products for defects, wear, and deviations from specifications. May use precision measuring instruments and complex test equipment.

label: Jewelers and Precious Stone and Metal Workers
hint: Design, fabricate, adjust, repair, or appraise jewelry, gold, silver, other precious metals, or gems.

label: Gem and Diamond Workers
hint: Fabricate, finish, or evaluate the quality of gems and diamonds used in jewelry or industrial tools.

label: Dental Laboratory Technicians
hint: Construct and repair full or partial dentures or dental appliances.

label: Medical Appliance Technicians
hint: Construct, maintain, or repair medical supportive devices such as braces, orthotics and prosthetic devices, joints, arch supports, and other surgical and medical appliances.

label: Ophthalmic Laboratory Technicians
hint: Cut, grind, and polish eyeglasses, contact lenses, or other precision optical elements. Assemble and mount lenses into frames or process other optical elements. Includes precision lens polishers or grinders, centerer-edgers, and lens mounters.

label: Packaging and Filling Machine Operators and Tenders
hint: Operate or tend machines to prepare industrial or consumer products for storage or shipment. Includes cannery workers who pack food products.

label: Painting, Coating, and Decorating Workers
hint: Paint, coat, or decorate articles, such as furniture, glass, plateware, pottery, jewelry, toys, books, or leather.

label: Coating, Painting, and Spraying Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
hint: Set up, operate, or tend spraying or rolling machines to coat or paint any of a wide variety of products, including glassware, cloth, ceramics, metal, plastic, paper, or wood, with lacquer, silver, copper, rubber, varnish, glaze, enamel, oil, or rust-proofing materials. Includes painters of transportation vehicles such as painters in auto body repair facilities.

label: Semiconductor Processing Technicians
hint: Perform any or all of the following functions in the manufacture of electronic semiconductors: load semiconductor material into furnace; saw formed ingots into segments; load individual segment into crystal growing chamber and monitor controls; locate crystal axis in ingot using x-ray equipment and saw ingots into wafers; and clean, polish, and load wafers into series of special purpose furnaces,

label: Photographic Process Workers and Processing Machine Operators
hint: Perform work involved in developing and processing photographic images from film or digital media. May perform precision tasks such as editing photographic negatives and prints.

label: Computer Numerically Controlled Tool Operators
hint: Operate computer-controlled tools, machines, or robots to machine or process parts, tools, or other work pieces made of metal, plastic, wood, stone, or other materials. May also set up and maintain equipment.

label: Computer Numerically Controlled Tool Programmers
hint: Develop programs to control machining or processing of materials by automatic machine tools, equipment, or systems. May also set up, operate, or maintain equipment.

label: Adhesive Bonding Machine Operators and Tenders
hint: Operate or tend bonding machines that use adhesives to join items for further processing or to form a completed product. Processes include joining veneer sheets into plywood; gluing paper; or joining rubber and rubberized fabric parts, plastic, simulated leather, or other materials.

label: Cleaning, Washing, and Metal Pickling Equipment Operators and Tenders
hint: Operate or tend machines to wash or clean products, such as barrels or kegs, glass items, tin plate, food, pulp, coal, plastic, or rubber, to remove impurities.

label: Cooling and Freezing Equipment Operators and Tenders
hint: Operate or tend equipment such as cooling and freezing units, refrigerators, batch freezers, and freezing tunnels, to cool or freeze products, food, blood plasma, and chemicals.

label: Etchers and Engravers
hint: Engrave or etch metal, wood, rubber, or other materials. Includes such workers as etcher-circuit processors, pantograph engravers, and silk screen etchers.

label: Molders, Shapers, and Casters, Except Metal and Plastic
hint: Mold, shape, form, cast, or carve products such as food products, figurines, tile, pipes, and candles consisting of clay, glass, plaster, concrete, stone, or combinations of materials.

label: Stone Cutters and Carvers, Manufacturing
hint: Cut or carve stone according to diagrams and patterns.

label: Glass Blowers, Molders, Benders, and Finishers
hint: Shape molten glass according to patterns.

label: Potters, Manufacturing
hint: Operate production machines such as pug mill, jigger machine, or potter's wheel to process clay in manufacture of ceramic, pottery and stoneware products.

label: Paper Goods Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
hint: Set up, operate, or tend paper goods machines that perform a variety of functions, such as converting, sawing, corrugating, banding, wrapping, boxing, stitching, forming, or sealing paper or paperboard sheets into products.

label: Tire Builders
hint: Operate machines to build tires.

label: Helpers--Production Workers
hint: Help production workers by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include supplying or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

label: Production Workers, All Other
hint: All production workers not listed separately.

label: Aircraft Cargo Handling Supervisors
hint: Supervise and coordinate the activities of ground crew in the loading, unloading, securing, and staging of aircraft cargo or baggage. May determine the quantity and orientation of cargo and compute aircraft center of gravity. May accompany aircraft as member of flight crew and monitor and handle cargo in flight, and assist and brief passengers on safety and emergency procedures. Includes loadmaste

label: First-Line Supervisors of Helpers, Laborers, and Material Movers, Hand
hint: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of helpers, laborers, or material movers, hand.

label: Recycling Coordinators
hint: Supervise curbside and drop-off recycling programs for municipal governments or private firms.

label: First-Line Supervisors of Material-Moving Machine and Vehicle Operators
hint: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of material-moving machine and vehicle operators and helpers.

label: First-Line Supervisors of Passenger Attendants
hint: Supervise and coordinate activities of passenger attendants.

label: First-Line Supervisors of Transportation Workers, All Other
hint: All first-line supervisors of transportation workers not listed separately.

label: Airline Pilots, Copilots, and Flight Engineers
hint: Pilot and navigate the flight of fixed-wing aircraft, usually on scheduled air carrier routes, for the transport of passengers and cargo. Requires Federal Air Transport certificate and rating for specific aircraft type used. Includes regional, national, and international airline pilots and flight instructors of airline pilots.

label: Commercial Pilots
hint: Pilot and navigate the flight of fixed-wing aircraft on nonscheduled air carrier routes, or helicopters. Requires Commercial Pilot certificate. Includes charter pilots with similar certification, and air ambulance and air tour pilots. Excludes regional, national, and international airline pilots.

label: Air Traffic Controllers
hint: Control air traffic on and within vicinity of airport, and movement of air traffic between altitude sectors and control centers, according to established procedures and policies. Authorize, regulate, and control commercial airline flights according to government or company regulations to expedite and ensure flight safety.

label: Airfield Operations Specialists
hint: Ensure the safe takeoff and landing of commercial and military aircraft. Duties include coordination between air-traffic control and maintenance personnel, dispatching, using airfield landing and navigational aids, implementing airfield safety procedures, monitoring and maintaining flight records, and applying knowledge of weather information.

label: Flight Attendants
hint: Monitor safety of the aircraft cabin. Provide services to airline passengers, explain safety information, serve food and beverages, and respond to emergency incidents.

label: Ambulance Drivers and Attendants, Except Emergency Medical Technicians
hint: Drive ambulance or assist ambulance driver in transporting sick, injured, or convalescent persons. Assist in lifting patients.

label: Driver/Sales Workers
hint: Drive truck or other vehicle over established routes or within an established territory and sell or deliver goods, such as food products, including restaurant take-out items, or pick up or deliver items such as commercial laundry. May also take orders, collect payment, or stock merchandise at point of delivery.

label: Heavy and Tractor-Trailer Truck Drivers
hint: Drive a tractor-trailer combination or a truck with a capacity of at least 26,001 pounds Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW). May be required to unload truck. Requires commercial drivers' license. Includes tow truck drivers.

label: Light Truck Drivers
hint: Drive a light vehicle, such as a truck or van, with a capacity of less than 26,001 pounds Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), primarily to pick up merchandise or packages from a distribution center and deliver. May load and unload vehicle.

label: Bus Drivers, School
hint: Drive a school bus to transport students. Ensure adherence to safety rules. May assist students in boarding or exiting.

label: Bus Drivers, Transit and Intercity
hint: Drive bus or motor coach, including regular route operations, charters, and private carriage. May assist passengers with baggage. May collect fares or tickets.

label: Shuttle Drivers and Chauffeurs
hint: Drive a motor vehicle to transport passengers on a planned or scheduled basis. May collect a fare. Includes nonemergency medical transporters and hearse drivers.

label: Taxi Drivers
hint: Drive a motor vehicle to transport passengers on an unplanned basis and charge a fare, usually based on a meter.

label: Motor Vehicle Operators, All Other
hint: All motor vehicle operators not listed separately.

label: Locomotive Engineers
hint: Drive electric, diesel-electric, steam, or gas-turbine-electric locomotives to transport passengers or freight. Interpret train orders, electronic or manual signals, and railroad rules and regulations.

label: Rail Yard Engineers, Dinkey Operators, and Hostlers
hint: Drive switching or other locomotive or dinkey engines within railroad yard, industrial plant, quarry, construction project, or similar location.

label: Railroad Brake, Signal, and Switch Operators and Locomotive Firers
hint: Operate or monitor railroad track switches or locomotive instruments. May couple or uncouple rolling stock to make up or break up trains. Watch for and relay traffic signals. May inspect couplings, air hoses, journal boxes, and hand brakes. May watch for dragging equipment or obstacles on rights-of-way.

label: Railroad Conductors and Yardmasters
hint: Coordinate activities of switch-engine crew within railroad yard, industrial plant, or similar location. Conductors coordinate activities of train crew on passenger or freight trains. Yardmasters review train schedules and switching orders and coordinate activities of workers engaged in railroad traffic operations, such as the makeup or breakup of trains and yard switching.

label: Subway and Streetcar Operators
hint: Operate subway or elevated suburban trains with no separate locomotive, or electric-powered streetcar, to transport passengers. May handle fares.

label: Rail Transportation Workers, All Other
hint: All rail transportation workers not listed separately.

label: Sailors and Marine Oilers
hint: Stand watch to look for obstructions in path of vessel, measure water depth, turn wheel on bridge, or use emergency equipment as directed by captain, mate, or pilot. Break out, rig, overhaul, and store cargo-handling gear, stationary rigging, and running gear. Perform a variety of maintenance tasks to preserve the painted surface of the ship and to maintain line and ship equipment. Must hold gover

label: Captains, Mates, and Pilots of Water Vessels
hint: Command or supervise operations of ships and water vessels, such as tugboats and ferryboats. Required to hold license issued by U.S. Coast Guard.

label: Motorboat Operators
hint: Operate small motor-driven boats. May assist in navigational activities.

label: Ship Engineers
hint: Supervise and coordinate activities of crew engaged in operating and maintaining engines, boilers, deck machinery, and electrical, sanitary, and refrigeration equipment aboard ship.

label: Bridge and Lock Tenders
hint: Operate and tend bridges, canal locks, and lighthouses to permit marine passage on inland waterways, near shores, and at danger points in waterway passages. May supervise such operations. Includes drawbridge operators, lock operators, and slip bridge operators.

label: Parking Attendants
hint: Park vehicles or issue tickets for customers in a parking lot or garage. May park or tend vehicles in environments such as a car dealership or rental car facility. May collect fee.

label: Automotive and Watercraft Service Attendants
hint: Service automobiles, buses, trucks, boats, and other automotive or marine vehicles with fuel, lubricants, and accessories. Collect payment for services and supplies. May lubricate vehicle, change motor oil, refill antifreeze, or replace lights or other accessories, such as windshield wiper blades or fan belts. May repair or replace tires.

label: Aircraft Service Attendants
hint: Service aircraft with fuel. May de-ice aircraft, refill water and cooling agents, empty sewage tanks, service air and oxygen systems, or clean and polish exterior.

label: Traffic Technicians
hint: Conduct field studies to determine traffic volume, speed, effectiveness of signals, adequacy of lighting, and other factors influencing traffic conditions, under direction of traffic engineer.

label: Transportation Inspectors
hint: Inspect equipment or goods in connection with the safe transport of cargo or people. Includes rail transportation inspectors, such as freight inspectors, rail inspectors, and other inspectors of transportation vehicles not elsewhere classified.

label: Aviation Inspectors
hint: Inspect aircraft, maintenance procedures, air navigational aids, air traffic controls, and communications equipment to ensure conformance with Federal safety regulations.

label: Transportation Vehicle, Equipment and Systems Inspectors, Except Aviation
hint: Inspect and monitor transportation equipment, vehicles, or systems to ensure compliance with regulations and safety standards.

label: Passenger Attendants
hint: Provide services to ensure the safety of passengers aboard ships, buses, trains, or within the station or terminal. Perform duties such as explaining the use of safety equipment, serving meals or beverages, or answering questions related to travel.

label: Transportation Workers, All Other
hint: All transportation workers not listed separately.

label: Conveyor Operators and Tenders
hint: Control or tend conveyors or conveyor systems that move materials or products to and from stockpiles, processing stations, departments, or vehicles. May control speed and routing of materials or products.

label: Crane and Tower Operators
hint: Operate mechanical boom and cable or tower and cable equipment to lift and move materials, machines, or products in many directions.

label: Dredge Operators
hint: Operate dredge to remove sand, gravel, or other materials in order to excavate and maintain navigable channels in waterways.

label: Hoist and Winch Operators
hint: Operate or tend hoists or winches to lift and pull loads using power-operated cable equipment.

label: Industrial Truck and Tractor Operators
hint: Operate industrial trucks or tractors equipped to move materials around a warehouse, storage yard, factory, construction site, or similar location.

label: Cleaners of Vehicles and Equipment
hint: Wash or otherwise clean vehicles, machinery, and other equipment. Use such materials as water, cleaning agents, brushes, cloths, and hoses.

label: Laborers and Freight, Stock, and Material Movers, Hand
hint: Manually move freight, stock, luggage, or other materials, or perform other general labor. Includes all manual laborers not elsewhere classified.

label: Recycling and Reclamation Workers
hint: Prepare and sort materials or products for recycling. Identify and remove hazardous substances. Dismantle components of products such as appliances.

label: Machine Feeders and Offbearers
hint: Feed materials into or remove materials from machines or equipment that is automatic or tended by other workers.

label: Packers and Packagers, Hand
hint: Pack or package by hand a wide variety of products and materials.

label: Stockers and Order Fillers
hint: Receive, store, and issue merchandise, materials, equipment, and other items from stockroom, warehouse, or storage yard to fill shelves, racks, tables, or customers' orders. May operate power equipment to fill orders. May mark prices on merchandise and set up sales displays.

label: Gas Compressor and Gas Pumping Station Operators
hint: Operate steam-, gas-, electric motor-, or internal combustion-engine driven compressors. Transmit, compress, or recover gases, such as butane, nitrogen, hydrogen, and natural gas.

label: Pump Operators, Except Wellhead Pumpers
hint: Tend, control, or operate power-driven, stationary, or portable pumps and manifold systems to transfer gases, oil, other liquids, slurries, or powdered materials to and from various vessels and processes.

label: Wellhead Pumpers
hint: Operate power pumps and auxiliary equipment to produce flow of oil or gas from wells in oil field.

label: Refuse and Recyclable Material Collectors
hint: Collect and dump refuse or recyclable materials from containers into truck. May drive truck.

label: Tank Car, Truck, and Ship Loaders
hint: Load and unload chemicals and bulk solids, such as coal, sand, and grain, into or from tank cars, trucks, or ships, using material moving equipment. May perform a variety of other tasks relating to shipment of products. May gauge or sample shipping tanks and test them for leaks.

label: Material Moving Workers, All Other
hint: All material moving workers not listed separately.

label: Air Crew Officers
hint: Perform and direct in-flight duties to ensure the successful completion of combat, reconnaissance, transport, and search and rescue missions. label: Aircraft Launch and Recovery Officers
hint: Plan and direct the operation and maintenance of catapults, arresting gear, and associated mechanical, hydraulic, and control systems involved primarily in aircraft carrier takeoff and landing operations. label: Armored Assault Vehicle Officers
hint: Direct the operation of tanks, light armor, and amphibious assault vehicle units during combat situations on land or in aquatic environments. label: Artillery and Missile Officers
hint: Manage personnel and weapons operations to destroy enemy positions, aircraft, and vessels. Duties include planning, targeting, and coordinating the tactical deployment of field artillery and air defense artillery missile systems units; directing the establishment and operation of fire control communications systems; targeting and launching intercontinental ballistic missiles; directing the storage

label: Command and Control Center Officers
hint: Manage the operation of communications, detection, and weapons systems essential for controlling air, ground, and naval operations. label: Infantry Officers
hint: Direct, train, and lead infantry units in ground combat operations. label: Special Forces Officers
hint: Lead elite teams that implement unconventional operations by air, land, or sea during combat or peacetime. These activities include offensive raids, demolitions, reconnaissance, search and rescue, and counterterrorism. In addition to their combat training, special forces officers often have specialized training in swimming, diving, parachuting, survival, emergency medicine, and foreign languages.

label: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders, All Other
hint: All military officer special and tactical operations leaders not listed separately.

label: First-Line Supervisors of Air Crew Members
hint: Supervise and coordinate the activities of air crew members. Supervisors may also perform the same activities as the workers they supervise.

label: First-Line Supervisors of Weapons Specialists/Crew Members
hint: Supervise and coordinate the activities of weapons specialists/crew members. Supervisors may also perform the same activities as the workers they supervise.

label: First-Line Supervisors of All Other Tactical Operations Specialists
hint: Supervise and coordinate the activities of all other tactical operations specialists not classified separately above. Supervisors may also perform the same activities as the workers they supervise.
